entries.name: step 3: the late block's dials, part 1 on the published snap picture, and the readings the step needs before any of its runs
entries.reason: Question 19's Wait holds 'until the pre-snap phase gives real spots' (ADR-089:558, :5). ADR-090, approved with question 4 Yes, gives them: its step 0 is on main, its step 1 carries the picture on the calls (S5) and publishes it on PLAY_START (S1, S2), and its step 2 is this step, proved by these checks with 'M8's table for his snap row' replaced by 'his published snap spot' (ADR-090 §7). The filed part-1 clause names Wait, a Mug-off arm and M8's partner reading of a passed-off man, which this step's hand-off fix removes; the filed monotone clause fails for Speed alone under the filed D18, found at step 0 and reported (pocketFreeRun.test.ts); the late block's t_e and w were filed CHOSEN with no values (rules.lateBlock). Each is settled here, before any pocket-1.s3 run, so nothing is chosen after a look.

lateBlock.provenance: CHOSEN, football judgement, no measurement; shown to the owner before any pocket-1.s3 run
lateBlock.why: t_e: a back stepping up meets a blitzer about 1.0 to 1.4 s after the snap, and a twist's exchange is missed by the first half second after its 0.5 s; 1.0 s is the first tick after both. w: at theta 11, k 2 and beta 0.5 the late block breaks a median 0.83 s after t_e (quartiles 0.53 and 1.17 s at m 8), so its beat tick is 1.5 s about one time in four, 2.0 s two in five, 2.5 s one in four and 3.0 s or later about one in ten; with the engine's travel a beaten man reaches the quarterback at about 2.5 to 3.5 s on the interior (median 3.0 s) and 0.5 to 2.0 s later on the edge, by move and depth, about a second after today's touched men (2.0 and 2.5 s) and before revision 1's 'Later' (about 4.0 s), which the stand-ins' reading (b) used.
lateBlock.shapeS: T = t_e + w * theta * exp(-beta * m / 41) * E^(1/k), m = -(the touching CHECK's margin), 1 to 19; E drawn once on fork beat/<the touching CHECK's rngLabel> after every pickup and stunt CHECK is written, and published then as a pass_rush_beat CHECK (actors [rusher, toucher], margin m, tier of m, rollRef the touching CHECK, testsAttrs empty). No CHECK, tick or threat for him before t_e; from t_e dieless pass_rush_ticks naming the late beat, the margin m capped at 0 before the beat tick and raised to RUSHER_WINS_REP's floor from it; no push window.
lateBlock.shapeL: From t_e each tick draws two d100s, rush/t<tick>/<rusherId>:late and rush/t<tick>/<toucherId>:late, and jitter = round((rusher - toucher) / repJitter.divisor) as today's tick jitter; margin = Math.round(Math.min(t - t_e, w * R) * (m + jitter) / (w * R)) + 0, the form of today's L margin. Each is a rolled pass_rush_tick with roll and opposedRoll, rollRef the touching CHECK. Reachable only once petition P17's doc text is in contracts.
lateBlock.beaten: His threat keeps his origin (PICKUP_LOST or STUNT_LOOPER) and band; its rollRef names the touching CHECK; its approach is ARC if EDGE and THROUGH if INTERIOR (row 3 of the approach card as built); D21 reads his time as the beat tick (S) or the first RUSHER_WINS_REP tick (L) plus the travel the engine gives a won rep from his alignment, his plan's move and his position.
lateBlock.toucher: RAN_THROUGH: the back the pickup assigned to him, the first actor of the blitz_pickup CHECK his record names. LATE_EXCHANGE: the looper's blocker in the plans the stunt CHECK was rolled on. A carried record keeps its toucher, so on a carried record the late beat's first actor is the carrier, not the CHECK's rusher.
lateBlock.invariant: every free-run time on both base corpora is later than t_e (fastest published 1.3 s); held by a unit grid test, never by a throw in play

rule.untouchedExchange: A LATE_EXCHANGE whose looper had no blocker (the stunt CHECK rolled with no adjacent blocker) was touched by nobody (D19's words): he runs on the free-run clock as a LOOPER_FREE man does, with no delay; his origin, band and labels are unchanged, and he is counted on every arm.

part1.arms: each arm against its own published picture; an arm that holds an input at a filed reference substitutes that reference and nothing else

monotone.graded: at the published tenth: one point more Acceleration is never later; one point more of both Speed and Acceleration is never later; the deeper of the card's drops is never sooner; over every man nobody touched on the design and pricing arms and over the unit grid (paths 3 to 14 yards, ratings 0 to 99, set, DELAYED and moving starts)

monotone.why: D18's start is relative to Speed (tau = 0.77 - 0.007 (Acceleration - Speed)), so one point of Speed alone can lengthen the start more than it shortens the run, by under 0.002 s, which changes a published tenth on about 158 of 504,900 grid pairs; D18 is filed and never fitted, so the literal clause would report a build fault no build can fix

The base-map entry's reason and its record, G.9, say which, as S3 stood when it was filed. Each arm's caller draws the picture its physics reads, and the engine reads only the picture its calls carry.
rule.references: The arms that vary one input hold the others at: Speed 50 and Acceleration 50; drop 5.0 yards; spot by group, depth and width from the ball, down lineman (1.0, 2.5), linebacker (2.5, 2.5), defensive back (5.0, 7.0). A held man is set (no moving start), keeps his alignment's bend and any DELAYED wait, and a held looper's crossing leg is the filed 0.5 yard. CHOSEN, information only, never a design value.
rule.freeRunKey: At step 3, 'free runner' in the miss rule's split (n, f, the quick split, the quick share's origin) means a man on the free-run clock under the arm's own reading (D19 on the design; every free runner under reading (c); UNBLOCKED only under reading (a)). The class is read on each seed set, and both are named when they differ.

entries.name: sight by looks: a pocket_sense CHECK per look, at the snap, when his blocker is beaten and every half second after, with memory; the alarm at the first decision after the look that registers him (D20 overruled); D36 for picks that share a tick
entries.reason: The owner overruled default D20 and the one pocket_sense roll per threat (G.7 item 2's question, answered at 2026-10-31T01:44:06Z): sight is several looks, the first at the snap, and a man seen at the snap sets off the alarm on the first tick. s7.earlyShare keeps its band and its words; its comparator M7 is restated as the share of FRONT and SIDE threats registered more than 0.5 s out over the looks each would get to the etaTick published at his creation, since the filed M7 is one roll with band edges the rule no longer has. The bands of s7.pressure, s7.sack and s7.hitOrSack are kept, though their stand-in basis (TOT §8.6) fired the free-runner alarm at D20's moment with sight a flat 0.9; the ruling moves those alarms earlier, so a step-7 miss on them is read first against the one-roll information arm. D36, the Orchestrator's default for picks that share a tick, fills a gap revision 2 already had and is shown to the owner, not asked.

ownersWord.words: For the first question, there should be multiple awareness rolls. Yes, at the snap. But at other points along the way.

question.words: When should a loose rusher he sees set off his first reaction: one second away (my default) or at the snap? This only matters by step 7.

reading.words: He gets a look at the snap. After that he gets another look every half second while a rusher he hasn't spotted is still coming. Each look is an awareness roll. A rusher in front of him is easier to spot than one from the side, and one from behind is hardest. The closer the rusher gets, the easier he is to spot. The moment he spots a rusher, his first reaction starts: step up, slide, run, try to make him miss, or keep reading and throw if someone's open. Once he spots a rusher, he keeps tracking him. A rusher he never spots only gets him at contact. This holds for every rusher, not only loose ones. A man who beats his blocker gets looked for from that moment on. It's built at step 7, so nothing changes in games now. If you'd rather the looks come at set moments instead, say the snap, the top of his drop and his hitch, tell me.
reading.status: the Orchestrator's reading, told to the owner; the owner may still switch to set moments (the snap, the top of his drop, his hitch) by a later named entry filed before step 7

beyondTheReading: a man he sends past him (a step-up under an ARC, or a won dodge) comes round behind him and must be spotted again (revision 2's :return; the owner's page, TMP:33)
a man first spotted within half a second gets no early reaction: his first reaction is must act's, with one read fewer (revision 2's LATE)
D36, the Orchestrator's default for picks that share a tick
ownersWord.unanswered: the message's second item, the pressure-to-sack PR hold, which this answer does not touch

looks.snap: every threat on the list at the snap, at t0.0, judged on his remaining time then
looks.beat: a threat created after the snap, on the line battle that creates him (tick s), judged on his remaining time at s; he enters the list at s + 0.5
looks.ticks: EVERY_TICK: at the top of each later half-second tick while he is live, unregistered and not yet arrived; no look on or after the tick he arrives (remaining time 0 or less)
looks.return: a man who comes round behind him (a step-up under an ARC, or a won dodge) is unregistered; one look at the tick of the move on :return with the BEHIND term, unless he already had a look on that tick; then :sense on each later tick, with the BEHIND term
looks.perRusherPerTick: at most one look a rusher a tick: the snap or beat :sense, a top-of-tick :sense, or a :return
looks.orderWithinTick: nearest remaining time first, then rusherId
looks.rusherNotRecord: sight belongs to the rusher, not to a threat record: a record that replaces his live one (the sooner arrival of a re-won rep) is not a creation, gets no beat look and keeps his registration and his from; a PUSH whose block breaks stays registered

closeness.grid: his remaining time rounded UP to the half second
closeness.integerForm: r10 = round((etaTick - tick) x 10); g = ceil(r10 / 5) x 5; closeness = 2 x (10 - g)

lookBand.EARLY: registers him with more than 0.5 s left
lookBand.LATE: registers him with 0.5 s or less left

grade.EARLY: first registered more than 0.5 s before he is due
grade.LATE: first registered within 0.5 s: no alarm; his first reaction is must act's, with one read fewer
grade.NEVER: no look registers him before contact: no choice at contact, QB_HIT.seen false; never a CHECK band
grade.none: on the stream, a threat whose play ends before any look registers him and before any contact has no grade, and is reported apart

rule.memory: registered for the rest of the play, except a man who comes round behind him; contact does not register him, so a shed man no look has registered keeps getting looks

noLook.PUSH: registered with no die from the push window's first report, EARLY
noLook.BLOCKED: no look; whether he checked such men comes from the movement roll's band

target.construct: nearest 0.90, threat-weighted over FRONT and SIDE, ties to the lower

alarm.moment: the first decision after the look that registers him EARLY: tick 0.5 for the snap look, the tick he enters the list (s + 0.5) for the beat look, the look's own tick for a top-of-tick look
alarm.push: the first status tick after the push window's first report, as revision 2 files it
alarm.perRusher: once a play, as revision 2's 'once per registered threat'; a man registered again after a return sets off no second alarm

D36.status: Orchestrator default, shown to the owner, not asked; not part of the owner's ruling
D36.alarmWithMustAct: when a man's alarm and must act fall on the same tick he makes one pick, must act's; the alarm counts as fired and no :alarm CHECK is drawn
D36.alarmsOnOneTick: two or more alarms on one tick are picked one at a time, nearest etaTick first, then tunables.ts:1212's tie, then rusherId; each pick sees the moves before it

rule.M7: for each FRONT and SIDE threat on the step's design-arm streams (one per rusher per creation; a replacing record is folded into the live one), the chance that a look registers him more than 0.5 s out, exact over the 100 faces, counted over the looks he would get to the etaTick published at his creation, read on the half-second grid; a :return is judged on the etaTick at the move, and other changes to etaTick after creation are reported apart; by from-class, origin, lead and quarterback; LATE, NEVER, NEVER at contact, the miss at the first forcing tick, the share whose alarm comes before must act, and the looks per threat reported beside it

reportedBeside: the stream's realized share inside the play
realized against expected registrations over the :sense CHECKs drawn

rule.x3: revision 1's guard: the unshown played rush (its call and disguise) permuted with personnel and protection held fixed leaves every look's count, tick, label, margin and band unchanged; and each look's margin reads only his awareness, the trait, the threat's from-class and his remaining time
informationArms: ONE_ROLL_D20 (the Orchestrator's choice, reported only, never graded, paired on both seed sets): revision 2's single roll at creation with band edges 0 and -30 at its own M7 target, and D20's alarm moment
rollAudit: at most one look a rusher a tick (:sense or :return)
no :sense after registration except after a return
no look on or after the tick he arrives
no :alarm CHECK when the alarm counts as fired on must act's tick
at most one :alarm a rusher a play

entries.name: shape L's toucher die, one per pair: rush/t<tick>/<toucherId>:late:<rusherId>
entries.reason: Review CT-F7, the Orchestrator's ruling. AM-2's shape L draws the toucher's die on rush/t<tick>/<toucherId>:late, and fork is a pure function of its label (contracts/src/rng.ts:52), so a man who touched two rushers who are both blocked late would draw one die for both on each tick, and the two blocks would share a roll, which ADR-004's roll audit (engine/test/rollAccounting.test.ts) would fail, since every rngLabel in a play's event stream is unique; refusing such a play instead would also change what AM-2 says. The toucher's die is now one per pair, rush/t<tick>/<toucherId>:late:<rusherId>, and no play is refused. The rusher's die stays rush/t<tick>/<rusherId>:late, and nothing on shape S changes. AM-2's entry stays as filed: this entry changes its words through rule.amends. Shape L is refused in play until P17's doc text is in contracts (E4b), so no game has drawn either label; this is filed before C14, step 3's only arm on shape L, runs. A ruling on a label, shown to the owner, not asked.

shapeL.perPair: one toucher die a pair (toucher and rusher) a tick: a man who touched two rushers both blocked late draws a die for each, and no play is refused
shapeL.unchanged: everything else AM-2 files for shape L: the jitter from the two dice, the margin, the rolled pass_rush_tick with the rusher's die as roll and the toucher's as opposedRoll, and rollRef the touching CHECK

rule.P17: P17's doc text names the pair label: under shape L the ticks draw their jitter on <rusherId>:late and <toucherId>:late:<rusherId>
rule.filedBefore: C14, step 3's only arm on shape L; shape L stays refused in play until P17's doc text is in contracts (E4b), when the engine's late block and calibration's late-tick check take the pair label

entries.name: the guard at step 4: the design, its pricing arm and the motion alone against step 3's arms
entries.reason: AM-1 (Appendix F, F.11) reads the guard at steps 2 to 10 against the previous step's arm and requires each later step's map filed as a named entry before that step's arms run; this is step 4's. It maps the arms that can become the game and the arm the design prices alone on interceptions: the design (D1) against step 3's design (C1), its pricing arm (D2) against step 3's pricing arm (C2), and the motion alone on the pricing build (D6) against C2, because §8 prices the motion alone at step 4 (ADR-089:1287) and §6.4 puts its predictions on the pricing arm (ADR-089:1036). AM-1 left s4.motion.int to an entry filed before step 4 naming its base: its base is C2, and it is D6's league-wide reading under this rule, so the clause and the guard cannot disagree on one pair; its filed reading is printed beside. The release clock is the arm's own, as §8 files it: both mixes on the arm's rate table. A motion throw leaves at most 0.4725 s after its decision tick, so it never changes release bin; reading the base on tick-aligned rates and the arm on raw rates would add 0.18 to 0.23 points of allowance on an unchanged mix, which the sim cannot earn, so that reading is printed beside and never graded. Every other arm is information or contrast and is printed beside, unguarded. With nothing changed this map stops the step by chance about 13% of the time (47% if every arm were graded).

rule.laterBases: filed as a named entry before that step's arms run
rule.gradedArms: every arm in the step's map

entries.name: step 4: the arms the clauses read, the hit construct, the tilts' reading and the chosen values
entries.reason: Step 4's twenty clauses name their arms in words only, and three of them read a direction with no population or noise rule. This entry files, before any step-4 arm runs, which arm each clause reads, how a hit is counted, how the tilts are read, the thresholds of the two falsifiers, and the values the design leaves CHOSEN; it moves no band, word or pin. The tilt clauses gain a population, a count floor and a noise line, so they are superseded for that and nothing else.

readings.s4.contact.arm: D3: contact alone, untilted, on today's line at today's quarterback clock (A0's settings plus the contact block, kind T: today's movement and clock, the stem and count read as A0 plays them, approach labelled by shape S's rows over today's facts), against A0. The band's basis, pkA's contest-alone arm, ran on today's line at today's clock (release 1.264 s). D4, the same on A14 (the stand-in hold), is printed beside; on it the band is out of reach by construction (A14's sacks are 34.84 to 47.93 before contact).
readings.s4.motion.arm: D6: the motion alone on the pricing build (C2 plus throwExec.motion), against C2, for s4.motion.hits and s4.motion.curveRises (s4.motion.int under AM-6); D5 (the motion alone on C1) against C1, and D1 and D2 against their bases, printed beside. §6.4: 'Prediction, on the pricing arm.'
readings.s4.curve.weights: the curve's own denominator, aimed throws per bin; attempt-weighted printed beside. On a motion arm raw bins equal decision bins (rho at most 0.4725 s).
readings.hitConstruct: V1-42 per dropback, keyed on the play's stamp: under pocket-1.s4 a sack or a QB_HIT of any phase on a play ending in a pass attempt, each dropback once; under every earlier stamp the legacy stand-in. QB_HIT ARRIVAL is written under either step-4 block; on every s4 arm the stand-in's dropbacks equal those with a QB_HIT ARRIVAL or SHED or a sack (a build check). A QB_HIT SACK is its sack's own record and adds nothing (a sack ends in no pass attempt, and the sack already counts once); the folds count it in QB_HIT by phase and tie it to its RUSHER_SACKS contest. P7 as granted has four phases (ARRIVAL, THROWING, SHED, SACK) where §7's row lists three: SACK widened by name at the guardian's pre-review (G-6).
readings.s4.tilt.reading: Arms D9 (PUSH or BLOCKED), D10 (free-run clock) and D11 (BEHIND or NEVER), each one tilt alone, against D8 (contact alone on C2, untilted). Population: first rated :contest CHECKs whose rusher is of the class; :contest2 excluded. One reading per clause: both leagues and both seed sets summed, sacks per contact tilted minus untilted, with its binomial SE. Against its direction only when beyond 2 SE the wrong way; fewer than 30 contacts in the class on either side is unreadable, reported and never passed; per league and per set printed beside. The margin's direction is a unit proof (exact). Every s4 fold reads an arrival_contest's band, never its tier or margin: tier is the ladder's tier of the margin, independent of b, so at b other than 5 (D15, D16) and on :contest2 a tier can disagree with its band.
readings.s4.tilt.freeRun.key: AM-2's freeRunKey (D19's three origins by band, and the untouched exchange); the label-only count printed beside.
readings.D21.touched: the late block's continuous breaking time (S) or crossing time (L) plus his travel, as filed; AM-2's 'beat tick' describes the published etaTick. Under S the beat's T is read on the beat's own tick only; a win built on another tick (none under S as built) would read the grid time, and since no published fact names the beat's tick a run cannot count it, so the unit proof is the check. Under L a late block won on its first engaged tick starts its crossing from m = 0 (the late clock's own start, as the snap is the block clock's; D17 only), and a crossing the interpolation does not place inside (t - 0.5, t] reads the win's tick t, not the interval's low end (unreachable while a margin of 15 wins on its tick; a unit proof at both ends). On D14 (the half-second reading, information only) every contactSeconds is the grid time, as P7's text says.
readings.contactOrder: contacts on a held ball resolve in the half-second grid's order (etaTick, the priority alignment, the lower PlayerId); contactSeconds orders only the motion's race, compared in whole milliseconds; a threat not ARRIVED on the grid at decision tick t hits inside the motion when its contact time is at most t + rho. releaseSeconds is published in whole milliseconds (P8's text), the race's unit; contactSeconds is published as computed. The grid order's alignment step names the priority alignment only: with two alignments, two different ones always include it, so the lower PlayerId breaks every remaining tie, as nearestThreat does. After a shed the threat list is rebuilt from the matchups as they stand after this tick's line battle, so a man who won his rep on this tick joins it (§4.5 item 6's 'rebuilt after any shed', read at the shed's tick); legacy, s1 to s3 and the motion alone keep the tick's list.
readings.chosen: rho0 0.3 s and rho_d 400 (rho 0.2275 to 0.4725 s; 0.325 at the flat league's 60); one tilt, strongest first: BEHIND or NEVER over a seen PUSH or BLOCKED over the free-run clock (NEVER over the engaged tilt is the design's); BEHIND is an ARC threat live when the quarterback steps up, from that STEP_UP on; a PUSH shed is 1.0 s on his existing threat with no new die; a contact's class is its strongest, and an arm with that class's tilt off plays it untilted, never under a weaker class's tilt (the classes partition the contacts, as s4.tilt.reading's population does); one THROWING QB_HIT a throw, the earliest; a QB_HIT SACK right after each RUSHER_SACKS contest, naming it by rollRef, and none on a sack with no contest (an escape caught, the horizon coverage sack, the motion alone). The dials' bounds are refusals, not choices: rho at least 0 and below one tick step (0.5 s) over the whole rating scale, b whole, tilt sizes at least 0, shed delays on the tenth, a second-arrival target from 0 to 100; the engine refuses them and calibration restates them (assertStep4Dials). The engine refuses a step-4 bundle at the top of each pass play, before that play's first die (a kickoff or run before the first pass play draws its dice, then the game throws and no stream escapes); calibration refuses before any game.
readings.motionReach: openness and clock runoff read at the decision tick; throwaways leave on their tick with no motion; no motion after an escape. The interception rules see the motion only through the IMMEDIATE accuracy row on a hit throw.
readings.contestChangesThrows: a shed lets him throw a ball that today is a sack, against §4.5's and §8's 'the contest changes no throw'; reported, with AM-6's declared prints.
readings.secondArrivalOff: D12: every arrival a rated :contest, keyed by tick and rusher. With it on, a :contest2 CHECK's target is the second arrival's (15) and its margin is roll.total minus that target, RUSHER_SACKS at margin 1 or more (16 or more on the die), where a :contest's target is b and RUSHER_SACKS is margin b or more; the folds read the band.
readings.s4.falsifier.release: release 40 against 80 on the flat league (every player; only a quarterback reads it), on D6's bundle, both seed sets; THROWING hits per 100 aimed throws; measurable means the difference (80 less 40), both seed sets summed, beyond 2 SE in its direction (more release, fewer hits), the SE being AM-1's independent binomial SE over aimed throws, the paired SE and each set printed beside. A paired gen probe (the home side's quarterback raised in every game, clamped at 99) printed beside.
readings.s4.falsifier.ratingProbes: exact at the contest for every b and tilt, and on a play-level probe replaying one contest with one rating raised; game-level paired probes printed with their SE (every quarterback's strength or agility, or every defense's four rushers' tackling or speed, raised 30); speed's effect on arrival printed separately; a rating falsifier NOT JUDGED is a structural failure.
readings.seedSets: bands graded on seed set 1 with set 2 beside, as at step 3; a band in on one set and out on the other is reported as split; directions as s4.tilt.reading; the guard as AM-6.
readings.missRule: no s4 clause is a miss-rule row; a miss is a failed prediction with both sets; no D31 class is printed. A falling curve records default D1's fallback at step 4 for step 5b's selection.
